app/package.json:6 — production start runs Nitro-built output (node .output/server/index.mjs), so the RC is load-bearing in production
app/vite.config.ts:2,6-7 — nitro() from nitro/vite wired into the build via plugins: [solidStart(), nitro()]

reach.rationale: One release-candidate API (Nitro v3) sits in the most central place possible — the production server runtime — but the rest of the stack is stable or recently-stable (SolidStart 2 stable 2026-08-04, Vite 8 stable 2026-03-12, router 1.0 = renumbered 0.16) and the app code itself uses nothing pre-stable. That's exactly the 'one or two / recently-stable in central places' middle of the scale.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6-7 — the only place the Nitro RC API is invoked; matches SolidStart v2's documented deployment-plugin seam
app/package.json:10 — the only dependency line touching the RC
app/src/lib/api.ts:1-6 — server data layer uses only plain fetch/Map and env access; no Nitro-specific imports
app/src/lib/queries.ts:1-9 — all six server queries route through @solidjs/router's stable query(), not Nitro primitives
containment.rationale: The pre-stable API is confined to vite.config.ts and package.json — precisely the seam SolidStart v2 docs say to swap deployment plugins at. The 13 source files under app/src contain zero framework-exotic surface, so a Nitro version bump or plugin swap touches two files.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6-7 — solidStart() + nitro() is verbatim the setup in SolidStart v2's docs (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/reference/entrypoints/vite-config), not a novelty choice

SPEC.md:30-33 — spec requires a self-hosted production server on $PORT; among Start v2's three documented deployment plugins (Nitro, Netlify, Cloudflare), only the portable Nitro satisfies it, and Nitro v3 exists only as beta/RC
app/src/entry-server.tsx:19-20 — mode "async" opts into renderToStringAsync, a reasonable stable choice over the default streaming mode for a straightforward data-heavy site
app/package.json — no experimental feature flags: Nitro experimental.tasks/islands and router deferStream are all absent (grep across app/src confirms)
justification.rationale: Nitro v3 RC buys something no stable API could: it is the framework-prescribed portable runtime for SolidStart v2, and no stable Nitro release is compatible with the Vite-8 plugin architecture. No other pre-stable API is used anywhere, and nothing is turned on for novelty.

findings.issue: The production server runtime is a release candidate (nitro ^3.0.261029-rc, published 2026-10-29, one day before review); Nitro v3 has shipped only alpha/beta/RC versions to date, so breaking changes and republish churn are possible.
findings.suggestion: Pin to a known-good RC (exact version, no caret) rather than floating on ^, and add a note/CI check to adopt nitro 3.0 stable the day it lands — given app/vite.config.ts:6-7 is the only integration point, the swap should be trivial.

findings.issue: The entire stack (SolidStart 2.1, router 1.0.1, Vite 8.3) stabilized only in the last 3-8 months, and reporting indicates SolidStart v2 is entering maintenance mode as the ecosystem focus shifts.
findings.suggestion: Keep dependency updates deliberate: re-run acceptance tests on minor bumps of @solidjs/start and nitro, and watch the SolidStart maintenance-announcement for migration paths.

summary: This is a deliberately conservative app on a deliberately new stack: every line of app code uses long-stable Solid/router primitives, and the single pre-stable dependency — Nitro v3 RC — is confined to package.json and vite.config.ts, exactly where SolidStart v2's documented deployment-plugin seam sits. The RC is justified: it's the only portable self-hosted runtime compatible with SolidStart v2's Vite-8 architecture. Risk is real but managed: one RC in the load-bearing position, and otherwise recently-stable (not experimental) framework releases.
